questions.question: If $P(E) = 0.05$, what is the probability of 'not $E$'?
The probability that a non-leap year has 53 Sundays is:
solutionSteps: Non-leap year has 365 days $= 52 \text{ weeks} + 1 \text{ day}$.
The extra day can be any of the 7 days of the week.
Probability of it being Sunday is 1/7.

questions.question:
A card is drawn from a deck of 52 cards. Find the probability that the card drawn is:
(i) a queen of black color
(ii) either a king or a queen
(iii) a spade
solutionSteps: (i) Black Queen: Spades and Clubs. Total 2. $P = 2/52 = 1/26$.
(ii) King or Queen: 4 Kings + 4 Queens. Total 8. $P = 8/52 = 2/13$.

questions.question:
Savita and Hamida are friends. What is the probability that both will have:
(i) the same birthday?
(ii) different birthdays? (ignoring leap year)
solutionSteps: (i) Same Birthday: Only 1 outcome where both share the day. $P = 1/365$.

questions.case_study: **PASSAGE:** Gaming Competition. In a school game, players draw two cards from a box containing cards numbered 1 to 20. The player wins if the product of the numbers on the two cards is a perfect square.

parts.i: If one card is drawn, what is the probability it is a prime number?
parts.ii: What is the probability that the number on the card is a multiple of 4?
parts.iii: If two cards are drawn (with replacement), find the probability that both have the same number (a doublet).
